note: Sat 14 Nov 2026 SGT run, verified against Fri 13 Nov US cash-equity close (latest completed session). This run's dominant development is that both inflation prints the market was watching this week came in confirming the hawkish turn rather than offering relief. (1) Oct core CPI (released Tue 10 Nov) printed +0.3% m/m for a third straight month (vs +0.2% consensus), headline +0.4% (vs +0.3%) -- this exactly matched Governor Waller's own stated threshold (delivered hours earlier) for considering a 50bp December move rather than 25bp. (2) Oct core PPI (released Fri 13 Nov) matched an already-elevated +0.3% m/m consensus with the y/y rate at 5.0% (highest since early 2023); headline PPI's y/y rate hit 6.5%, a roughly four-year high, even as the m/m pace cooled modestly versus an upwardly-revised prior. A broad chorus of Fed officials reinforced the hawkish tone through the week: Dallas Fed's Logan (a 2026 voter) wants 'at least two more' 25bp hikes; Boston Fed's Collins said 'additional firming' is appropriate 'soon'; San Francisco Fed's Daly said it's 'hard to say policy is restrictive enough'; Governor Bowman flagged inflation 'broadening' with her own estimate that core PCE moved up to ~3.3% y/y in October from 3.1% in September; only NY Fed's Williams (FOMC Vice Chair) struck a more measured tone, saying the Fed will act 'over time' without committing to a specific December move. CME FedWatch now prices 100% odds of a hike at the 9 Dec FOMC (~88.5% for 25bp, ~11.5% for 50bp), with a further hike also priced for January. Equities absorbed this in orderly fashion rather than capitulating: a weekly loss (S&P -0.40%, Nasdaq -0.91%) with VIX up 3.2% to 19.30 -- a cooling, not a disorderly risk-off, move. Gold's prior real-yield-driven rout paused (roughly flat, +0.16%) while silver extended its slide (-2.2%). The one clear structural de-escalation data point: China's MOFCOM confirmed (9 Nov) a further two-month extension of the rare-earth/battery/graphite export-control suspension through 10 Jan 2027, though the separate April-2025 licensing controls on dysprosium, terbium and yttrium remain in force. All 40 universe tickers plus the 9-ticker rare-earth basket refreshed this run; no new company-specific catalysts were identified within the rare-earth names this week, so those calls lean on the China-truce/structural-reshoring theme rather than fresh idiosyncratic news.
